summary: Ukraine experienced widespread drone and missile attacks across multiple regions including Kyiv, Odesa, and Kharkiv, with Russian forces claiming control of settlements in Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia regions. Ukraine's military leadership underwent significant changes with General Drapatyy appointed as new commander-in-chief and General Skibiuk as head of the General Staff. Additional developments include embezzlement in defense infrastructure projects, changes in U.S. military aid disbursement, and ongoing cross-border aerial activity.
key_points: Russian forces claimed control of Artelnoye in Kharkiv region and Blagovatnoye in Zaporizhzhia region. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31833)
Ukrainian President Zelensky appointed General Drapatyy as new commander-in-chief and General Skibiuk as head of the General Staff. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31836)
Multiple drone attacks reported across Kyiv, Odesa, Kharkiv, and other regions with air raid alerts activated. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69285)
68 million hryvnias embezzled during construction of anti-drone structures for energy facility in Nikolaev region. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31843)
U.S. Senate Representative Durbin announced $400 million in military aid delayed until fiscal year 2029 under new administration. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31820)
Russian Ministry of Defense reported strikes on Ukrainian ports, ships, and logistics centers. (Source: @tass_agency/386534)
Former Commander-in-Chief Zaluzhny holds 70% trust rating among Ukrainians, while Zelensky ranks fourth. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31834)
Russian forces established control over parts of Sumy region near border areas. (Source: @tass_agency/386569)

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces claimed control over settlements in Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia regions while conducting widespread drone and missile attacks across Ukraine. Ukraine underwent significant military leadership changes with General Drapatyy appointed as new commander-in-chief. Multiple infrastructure targets were struck, and defense-related corruption cases emerged alongside delays in U.S. military aid disbursement.
ukraine: President Zelensky appointed General Drapatyy as new commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, replacing Syrsky, with General Skibiuk taking over as head of the General Staff. Drapatyy, a Hero of Ukraine and knight of the Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky, previously commanded the 2nd Mechanized Battalion during the ATO in eastern Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/82828)

A survey by Rating Group showed President Zelensky ranked fourth in public trust ratings, while former Commander-in-Chief Zaluzhny led with 70% trust. The leadership transition occurred amid ongoing military challenges and public scrutiny of command decisions. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31834)

In the Nikolaev region, 68 million hryvnias were embezzled during construction of anti-drone structures for an energy facility. A 37-year-old director from Krivoy Rog received advance payments then transferred funds to controlled accounts without completing work. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31843)

Kyiv region came under attack with five private houses damaged in Bucha district. A man, woman, and three children were injured during the overnight strike on civilian infrastructure. (Source: @UkraineNow/82827)

Military commissars and police in Kiev forcibly drafted an elderly man from a bus, during which he lost consciousness. The incident highlights ongoing mobilization tensions and enforcement methods. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31842)

Lvov resident was forcibly taken into a TCC van by police officers and military commissars, illustrating continued mobilization enforcement actions across western Ukraine. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31818)
russia: Russian Ministry of Defense reported conducting strikes on Ukrainian ports, sea vessels, and logistics centers supporting Ukrainian forces throughout the day. These operations targeted maritime infrastructure and transportation hubs. (Source: @tass_agency/386534)
Military expert Andrey Marochko stated Russian forces control most of the settlement Pesarovka in Sumy region, indicating continued cross-border advances. (Source: @tass_agency/386569)
Russian forces claimed control of Artelnoye in Kharkiv region and Blagovatnoye in Zaporizhzhia region, expanding territorial gains in eastern Ukraine. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31833)

Russian Defense Ministry expanded contract opportunities for convicted citizens, allowing those with sentences for serious crimes including drug trafficking and smuggling to serve in special units. (Source: @tass_agency/386533)

Bloomberg reported Russia no longer intends to return occupied territories as part of potential peace agreements, planning to maintain them as buffer zones following Trump-Putin talks in Anchorage. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31826)
eastern_front: Russian forces claimed advances near Zaliznychny and Nikanorivka, with DeepStateUA updating maps to reflect territorial changes. These movements indicate ongoing positional warfare in the Donbas region. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23676)
Russian forces established control over parts of Sumy region near border areas, specifically reporting control of Pesarovka settlement. (Source: @tass_agency/386569)
Ukrainian military intelligence reported enemy drone activity near Rogan in Kharkiv region approaching from northern directions, maintaining pressure on frontline positions. (Source: @kpszsu/69671)
Russian air defense units from BARS-Sarmat detachment intercepted Ukrainian drones approaching cities in the Donetsk People's Republic using small arms fire. (Source: @tass_agency/386570)
northern_front: Air raid alerts were activated in Kyiv region near Baryshivka and in Chernihiv region with reports of enemy aircraft movement. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69306)
Drone activity detected along the border area between Kyiv and Chernihiv regions near Nova Basan, with potential threat to northern approaches. (Source: @eRadarrua/102146)
Chernihiv region reported one drone at Makovka reservoir and another near Ichnia/Pryluki, indicating continued northern axis pressure. (Source: @eRadarrua/102152)
Sumy region experienced one group of attack drones moving southwest toward Kharkiv region, maintaining cross-border threat dynamics. (Source: @eRadarrua/102167)
southern_front: Odesa region faced multiple missile attacks with two Onyx missiles reportedly targeting the port city and nearby Chornomorsk. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69299)
Two rockets struck Odesa, with additional threats reported for potential Iskander-M launches from Taganrog in Rostov region. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69293)
Drone activity detected over Kherson region moving west toward Velyka Oleksandrivka, maintaining pressure on southern front lines. (Source: @kpszsu/69715)
Four maritime drones approached Odesa port area with two additional drones coming from sea, plus four more from previous course toward Chornomorsk. (Source: @eRadarrua/102201)
Drone activity reported in Dnipropetrovsk region moving toward Tokmykivka, indicating continued southern axis pressure. (Source: @kpszsu/69713)
air_war: Multiple drone swarms attacked targets including a gas processing plant in Yefremovka, Kharkiv region, using Geranium-type unmanned aerial vehicles. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31819)
Kyiv region experienced air raid alerts with reports of attack drones near Baryshivka and potential threats in the capital's northern districts. (Source: @eRadarrua/102181)
Kharkiv region drone activity detected moving south-west from Rogan area, maintaining aerial pressure on industrial and residential targets. (Source: @kpszsu/69671)
Odesa region faced coordinated drone and missile attacks with threats of Iskander-M ballistic missile launches from southern-eastern directions. (Source: @eRadarrua/102145)
Poltava region reported northern drone activity moving toward Mirgorod, while Kirovograd region detected southern course drones, indicating broad aerial coverage. (Source: @kpszsu/69718)
key_developments: Russian forces claimed control of Artelnoye in Kharkiv region and Blagovatnoye in Zaporizhzhia region, expanding territorial holdings. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31833)
President Zelensky appointed General Drapatyy as new commander-in-chief and General Skibiuk as head of the General Staff in major leadership reshuffle. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31836)
Widespread drone and missile attacks struck Kyiv, Odesa, Kharkiv, and other regions with civilian casualties reported in Bucha district. (Source: @UkraineNow/82827)
68 million hryvnias embezzled during anti-drone structure construction in Nikolaev region, highlighting defense sector corruption. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31843)
U.S. Congress-approved $400 million military aid delayed until 2029 under incoming administration, affecting immediate supply chains. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31820)
Russian Defense Ministry expanded contract recruitment to include convicted citizens for serious crimes serving in special units. (Source: @tass_agency/386533)
Bloomberg reported Russia abandoning territorial concessions, planning to retain occupied areas as buffer zones post-peace negotiations. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31826)
sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces maintain offensive momentum with territorial gains in Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia regions while conducting sustained drone campaigns across Ukraine's northern, eastern, and southern axes. The leadership changes in Ukraine's military command present both opportunities for renewed operational focus and risks of disruption during transition periods. Delayed U.S. military aid creates vulnerabilities in ammunition supplies and equipment replacement cycles. Russian expansion of contract recruitment among convicted populations suggests manpower shortages in certain units. Cross-border drone activity from Sumy region indicates continued pressure on northern approaches to Kyiv.
sections.regional_response: European partners continue monitoring Ukraine's internal political transitions while managing refugee flows from affected regions. NATO members have increased air policing missions in response to expanded Russian aerial activity near allied borders. Regional energy infrastructure remains vulnerable to continued drone strikes targeting logistics hubs and processing facilities. International monitoring bodies are investigating reported corruption cases in defense procurement amid ongoing funding concerns. Diplomatic channels remain engaged on potential peace frameworks despite reported Russian rejection of territorial concessions.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian public trust ratings show declining confidence in presidential leadership relative to military commanders, potentially affecting domestic political stability. Russian media narratives emphasize territorial consolidation while downplaying casualty reports from ongoing operations. Commercial infrastructure targets like Wildberries distribution centers suggest hybrid warfare tactics extending beyond traditional military objectives. Mobilization enforcement actions reveal ongoing recruitment challenges and public resistance to conscription measures. Technical intelligence indicates continued refinement of drone warfare capabilities on both sides with emphasis on maritime and port facility targeting.
